newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian c.bank to order sovereign credit rating.
newsitem.headline: Estonian c.bank to order sovereign credit rating.

text.p: The Central Bank of Estonia said on Wednesday it had decided to order a credit rating for the Baltic state.

The issue has been controversial, with analysts saying a rating, likely to be of investment grade, would cause too many foreign funds to flow into Estonia and worsen what some see as an overheating economy.
The central bank said in a statement it hoped a credit rating would help to integrate Estonia's financial markets and raise the efficiency of local financial intermediaries.
"The international integration of Estonia's financial markets is an important precondition for long-term and continuous economic growth," it said.
"The free movement of capital and an efficient financial sector enable an open economy to direct its productive means to spheres where earnings are the highest," it added.
Baltic neighbour Latvia already has a rating, an investment grade BBB by Standard & Poor's, while Lithuania has a BBB- from Moodys.
A central bank spokesperson could not say when or how the rating could be ordered.
"The bank is certainly going to consider several offers," the spokesperson told Reuters.
The central bank warned that some of the problems which made it hesitate to get a rating, such as the rapid growth of bank credits and rising share prices, still existed.
But it said it was prepared to take measures to make sure that Estonia's economic development was stable.
"The central bank is therefore continuously ready to apply more stricter methods in monetary policy if guaranteeing balanced economic growth needs it," the bank said.
